newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate edges up on poor supply.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate edges up on poor supply.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rose 10 basis points to 10.9 percent on Friday amid very low supply of kuna funds on the money market.
Dealers said settlements shrank to 19 million from Thursday's 30.5 million kuna. Demand was 45 million kuna.
To improve liquidity, the central bank intervened by injecting 115.8 million kuna into the banking sector through a bill repo deal expiring on February 18.
Main interbank and insurer rates were steady.
The central bank calculated the kuna mid-rates for Saturday and next Monday weaker at 6.0140 against the dollar and 3.5662 against the German mark. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
